items.title: Commencement
notes:
A meeting of City Council was held at 3:09 p.m. this date, chaired by Mayor B. Vrbanovic. Notice of this meeting had been previously given to all members of Council by the City Clerk pursuant to Chapter 25 (Council Procedure) of the Municipal Code.

The meeting began with a Land Acknowledgement given by the Mayor.

items.title: Disclosure of Pecuniary Interest and the General Nature Thereof
Make It Kitchener 2.1, DSD-2026-196
notes:
Council considered Development Services Department report DSD-2026-196, entitled Make It Kitchener 2.1, dated  June 11, 2026, recommending approval of Make it Kitchener 2.1 the City's next Economic Development strategy, a continuation of Make it Kitchener 2.0. Cory Bluhm, Executive Director, Economic Development, presented the report and responded to questions from Council.  Jeremy Dueck, Director, Arts and Entertainment, was also in attendance to respond to questions from Council.

Sheldon McCormick, Communitech, addressed Council in support of Make It Kitchener 2.1 and the continued partnership with between Communitech and the City. S. McCormick provided highlights of a number of tech initiatives that Communitech, expressing appreciation for the continued support from the City of Kitchener. S. McCormick then responding to questions from Council. 

Councillor P. Singh left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

Councillor C. Michaud entered the meeting at this time.

C. Bluhm then responded to questions related to the focus areas for economic growth within the City, including the health network, food incubators, and support for federal defense initiatives, noting all of these initiatives continue to support growth within our community. In response to further questions, C. Bluhm noted in terms of comments raised related to food incubation, C. Bluhm noted staff take those away, noting that there were a number of limitations with the Municipal Act and they may not be able to proceed further on this initiative, but he provide a further response back to Council on that matter. 

Questions were raised about supporting businesses within the Downtown and whether there were further initiatives that could help to get new businesses off the ground.  C. Bluhm noted an upcoming business project for Economic Development includes a retail and restaurant attraction strategy for the downtown.

items.title: Development Charges Reduction Program, FIN-2026-256
notes:
Council considered Financial Services Department report FIN-2026-255, entitled Development Charges Reduction Program, dated June 10, 2026, recommending a Development Charges Reduction Program. Council was also in receipt of written submissions from Mattamy Homes and Cachet Homes related to this matter.

Councillor P. Singh left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

Councillor M. Johnston left and re-entered the meeting at this time.

Katie Fischer, Director, Financial Reporting and ERP Solutions, presented the report and responded to questions from Council. 

Councillor J. Deneault left and re-entered the meeting at this time

Councillor A. Owodunni let the meeting at this time.

In response to questions, K. Fischer advised the proposed program is a reduction of hard services DC, noting any additional reductions behind the proposed reduction would affect soft services and would have impacts to the tax base. K. Fischer stated, the proposed program is cost neutral, allowing for a reduction in Development charges for a three year period of time, that would also obtain grant funding from the provincial and federal governments to help off-set these costs. In response to further questions, K. Fischer advised the March 1, 2026 Canada Ontario Partnership to Build program date, aligns with a Provincial HST Incentive. 

Jonathan Lautenbach, Chief Financial Officer, was also in attendance to respond to questions from Council.

items.title: Mayoral Business and Updates - Mayor B. Vrbanovic
notes: Mayor B. Vrbanovic advised that the City would be issuing a media release today announcing our draft Water Allocation Policy - an important step to manage new water supply responsibly and transparently while continuing to support growth. Mayor Vrbanovic noted this follows the Region of Waterloo’s approval of its Interim Risk Management Framework and Regional Water Allocation Policy, which set the structure for allocating capacity and allow development activity to gradually resume across the region. It was noted Kitchener’s draft policy creates a clear and transparent approach to prioritize projects with the greatest community benefit - especially housing, including affordable housing, along with essential services and economic development. It also reflects strong collaboration with the Region, our municipal partners, and the development industry, and reinforces that Kitchener remains open for business, with applications continuing to be reviewed so projects are ready to move forward when water becomes available. Mayor Vrbanovic further advised today's media release shares the City's progress on this work with the community before a final version is brought forward for Council’s consideration later this month.

motions.text: "That Make It Kitchener 2.1, attached as Appendix A to Development Services Department report DSD-2026-196, be approved as an update to the original Make It Kitchener 2.0 strategy; and further; That Make It Kitchener 2.1, attached as Appendix A to Report DSD-2026-196, be used to guide the City’s future actions and investments in support of economic development, from 2026 to 2030."
